source_text: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ σωμάτων ἀνάστασιν ἔσεσθαι πεπιστεύκαμεν μετὰ τὴν τῶν ὅλων συντέλειαν, οὐχ ὡς οἱ Στωϊκοὶ δογματίζουσι κατά τινας κύκλων περιόδους, γινομένων ἀεὶ καὶ ἀπογινομένων τῶν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐπί τι χρήσιμον, ἅπαξ δέ, τῶν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς αἰώνων πεπερασμένων, καὶ εἰς τὸ παντελὲς διὰ μόγων τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν σύστασιν ἔσεσθαι χάριν κρίσεως. Δικάζουσι δὲ ἡμῖν οὐ Μίνως οὐδὲ Ῥαδάμανθυς, ὧν πρὸ τῆς τελευτῆς οὐδεμία τῶν ψυχῶν ὡς μυθολογοῦσιν ἐκρίνετο· δοκιμαστὴς δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ ποιητὴς θεὸς γίνεται. Κἂν γὰρ πάνυ φληνάφους καὶ σπερμολόγους ἡμᾶς νομίσητε, μέλον οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν, ἐπεὶ τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ πεπιστεύκαμεν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ οὐκ ὢν πρὶν ἢ γενέσθαι τίς ἤμην οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον, μόνον δὲ ἐν ὑποστάσει τῆς σαρκικῆς ὕλης ὑπῆρχον, γεγονὼς δὲ ὁ μὴ πάλαι διὰ τῆς γενέσεως τὸ εἶναι πεπίστευκα· τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ὁ γενόμενος καὶ διὰ θανάτου μηκέτι ὤν, αὖθίς τε μηκέθ᾿ ὁρώμενος, ἔσομαι πάλιν, ὥσπερ μὴ πάλαι γεγονὼς εἶτα γεννηθείς. Κἂν πῦρ ἐξαφανίσῃ μου τὸ σαρκίον, ἐξατμισθεῖσαν τὴν ὕλην ὁ κόσμος κεχώρηκεν· κἂν ἐν ποταμοῖς, κἂν ἐν θαλάτταις ἐκδαπανηθῶ, κἂν ὑπὸ θηρίων διασπασθῶ, ταμείοις ἐναπόκειμαι πλουσίου δεσπότου. Καὶ ὁ μὲν πτωχὸς καὶ ἄθεος οὐκ οἶδε τὰ ἀποκείμενα· θεὸς δὲ ὁ βασιλεύων, ὅτε βούλεται, τὴν ὁρατὴν αὐτῷ μόνῳ ὑπόστασιν ἀποκαταστήσει πρὸς τὸ ἀρχαῖον.
pass_a_gloss: And because of this we have believed that there will be a resurrection of bodies after the completion of all things, not as the Stoics dogmatize according to certain cycles, things always coming into being and passing away for no useful purpose, but once, since the ages pertaining to us have been completed, and the constitution will be for the sake of judgment through the deeds of men. And they do not judge us, neither Minos nor Rhadamanthus, since before their death none of the souls were judged as they mythologize; but the Creator God himself becomes the judge. And even if you consider us to be foolish and talkative, it is not a concern to us, since we have believed in this reason. For just as I was not before I came into being and did not know that I was, but only existed in the substance of fleshly matter, and having come into being I have believed in existence through birth; in the same way, the one who has come into being and through death is no longer, and will not be seen again, I will be again, just as if I had not come into being before and then was born. And even if fire destroys my flesh, the world has received the evaporated matter; and even if I am dissolved in rivers or in seas, or torn apart by beasts, I am stored in the treasuries of a rich Master. And the poor and godless man does not know the things that have been stored away; but God, the reigning King, when he wishes, will restore the visible substance, visible only to him, to its original state.

choices.english: will restore to its original state

pass_b_english: Because of this we have believed that a resurrection of bodies will take place after the completion of all things. It will not happen as the Stoics teach, through recurring cycles in which the same things endlessly come into being and pass away for no useful purpose. Rather, it will happen once, since the ages that pertain to us have been completed, and the reconstitution will occur for the sake of judgment through the deeds of men. We will not be judged by Minos or Rhadamanthus; before their death no souls were judged as the myths claim. Instead, the Creator God himself becomes the judge.

Even if you consider us foolish and babblers, it does not concern us, because we have believed in this reason. Just as I did not exist before I came into being and was unaware of myself, but only subsisted in the substance of fleshly matter, and having come into being I came to trust in existence through birth, so also the one who has come into being and through death is no longer, and will not be seen again, yet I will be again — just as if I had not existed before and then was born.

Even if fire consumes my flesh, the world has received the evaporated matter. Even if I am dissolved in rivers or in the sea, or torn apart by beasts, I am stored in the treasuries of a rich Master. The poor and godless man does not know what has been stored away. But God, the reigning King, when he wishes, will restore the visible substance — visible to him alone — to its original state.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between Stoic cyclicality and the singular Christian judgment, the ontological argument regarding existence and birth, and the metaphor of the stored treasure. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
